summary: [MERGED into TKT-110] Inventory's availability read emits a seconds-tier Cache-Control its OpenAPI contract never declares (TKT-128 ai-review)
description:
### Finding (TKT-128 ai-review, confirmed against the code)

Inventory's public availability read emits an ADR-004 **seconds-tier** TTL that its OpenAPI contract
does not declare:

- `services/inventory/internal/api/server.go:249` (`availability`) sets
  `Cache-Control: public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`.
- `services/inventory/api/openapi.yaml` — the `getAvailability` `'200'` response declares **no**
  `Cache-Control` header. `grep -ci cache-control` over that file returns **0**.

Catalog is the only service whose contract declares its tiers (17 hits, minutes + hours). Commerce,
payments and access declare none and emit none on domain reads (`no-store` default), which is
consistent. Inventory is the only mismatch: **real behaviour, no declaration.**

### Why it matters

[ADR-009](docs/adr/ADR-009-contract-first-apis.md) makes the OpenAPI document authoritative and the
gate diffs it, so an undeclared header is outside the gate's reach — nothing detects drift if that
`max-age=5` changes, disappears, or is copied wrong onto another route. And a future cache owner
(TKT-31) reading the contract to learn the tiers **will not find the seconds tier at all** — the one
tier where staleness is most load-bearing during an on-sale.

It is the inverse of the defect TKT-128 fixed in ADR-004: that was a declaration with no behaviour;
this is a behaviour with no declaration.

### Why it is not fixed in TKT-128

TKT-128's COS 5 forbids **any** source change in its diff, and this needs one (`openapi.yaml` plus a
regenerated `openapi_gen.go`). TKT-128 recorded the gap in ADR-004's amendment instead; this ticket
closes it.

### Scope

Declare the header on the `getAvailability` `'200'` response, matching how catalog declares its tiers
(`services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml`, the `CacheControl` response header component). Then
`make generate` and commit the regenerated `openapi_gen.go` **before** running the gate —
`check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift.

Worth checking in the same pass whether the seconds-tier value belongs in a named constant the way
catalog's `CacheControlPublicReads` / `CacheControlPublicVenueReads` are, rather than a literal at the
call site.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `getAvailability`'s `'200'` response declares `Cache-Control` in `services/inventory/api/openapi.yaml`.
- [ ] The declared value matches what the handler emits (`public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`).
- [ ] `openapi_gen.go` regenerated and committed; `make check` green.
- [ ] ADR-004 § Amendment (TKT-128)'s sentence recording this as an open gap is updated to say it is closed.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 validation — re-verified against HEAD `ac2952b`

**Still real.** `grep -ci cache-control services/inventory/api/openapi.yaml` = 0, while `services/inventory/internal/api/server.go:249` still emits `public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`. Behaviour with no declaration, unchanged.

**Verdict: still worth doing → Ready.** Not DoR-baked: the 8-item shaping happens when the ticket is claimed, per the owner's drain-the-debt call.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Merged into TKT-110 — do not claim

This ticket's scope now lives in **TKT-110** (Declare the responses catalog and inventory actually emit (lifecycle 400s + the availability cache tier)), which carries it verbatim under an *Absorbed TKT-137* section. Moved out of Ready so it cannot be picked up in parallel. Nothing was dropped — reopen this only if the merge is reversed at plan time.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### Closed as merged into TKT-110

Board validation 2026-08-08. This ticket's own summary has said `[MERGED into TKT-110]` since it was
folded in, but it was never transitioned — so it kept occupying Backlog and inflating the count of
outstanding work. **TKT-110 is Done**, verified before closing this.

No stage durations: the work was carried out under TKT-110 and its metrics belong there. This closure
is bookkeeping, not delivery.

**retro:** merging ticket B into ticket A needs to *close* B, not just retitle it. Six tickets
carried a `[MERGED into …]` marker in Backlog; the marker was written for a human reader and no
step ever acted on it. A summary prefix is not a state transition.
